Subject: Model-11A gradual drift — request: staged rollback & SLA carveout for FinVoy

Hi Lucille / FinVoy SRE,

We’re seeing a sustained, gradual increase in p95 latency for model-11a on FinVoy’s production traffic over the last 36 hours. It’s not a single spike — the trend is subtle but persistent, now crossing your SLA threshold (~+18% p95 vs baseline) during peak windows. Attached is a CSV with the rolling p95 and request traces.

We expect the root cause is increased headroom pressure from a change in token length distribution after Tuesday’s campaign (Rishi will confirm). Our immediate mitigation options: a) an immediate full rollback to model-10z (fast but higher Q-risk), or b) a staged rollback / traffic split to model-10z over a 3-hour window with small increments to limit user-visible regression.

Requesting authorization to execute option (b): a staged fallback starting at 5% traffic to model-10z, increasing by 15% every 30 minutes with automated health checks (latency and error rate) and a circuit-breaker if error-rate rises >0.5%. We also need a temporary SLA carveout for the maintenance window (3 hours) to avoid penalty triggers while we stabilize.

Please confirm asap — if you prefer an immediate full rollback we can do that within 12 minutes but would like signoff from FinVoy and Revenue Ops for any SLA exceptions.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Blake | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(j) +1 415-555-0132

Attachments: m11a-p95-trend.csv

Jordan —

Thanks for the quick heads up and the CSV. We’re seeing intermittent timeouts in a subset of our regional traffic as well (APIs returning 504s around peak). Our product team is worried about any functional regressions, but latency is becoming customer-visible.

A few clarifying questions before we sign off on staged rollback:
- Can you share the exact canary health checks and the criteria for halting the rollout?
- Do you have a rollback playbook if model-10z shows degraded output fidelity?
- What is the customer-visible window for each 15% increment? Our SREs want to coordinate monitoring and incident channels.

If you can provide the canary config and playbook we’ll aim to approve a staged approach within 2 hours. If we can’t get those safely, we’d prefer a short, controlled full rollback with close QA.

— Lucille
Lucille Park | Head of Platform, FinVoy
lucille@finvoy.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Model-11A gradual drift — request: staged rollback & SLA carveout for FinVoy

Lucille / team —

Quick technical note and attached playbook + canary config (canary-config.json, fallback-playbook.md). Summary:
- Root cause hypothesis: 15% increase in median prompt length for the payments flow (token expansion from additional metadata). That raises memory churn and increases tail latency on model-11a kernels under the current batching heuristic.
- Canary plan: start 5% → 20% traffic over 30-minute increments: 5%, 20%, 40%, 60%, 80%, 100% if health checks pass. Health checks: p95 (rolling 15m) must not degrade more than 5% relative to pre-rollout baseline; error rate must remain <0.1% absolute. Circuit-break: immediate pause + automated rollback to 100% model-11a if error rate >0.5% or if p95 worsens >20% at any step.
- Fallback plan: if fidelity issues appear on model-10z, we’ll pause traffic shift and run sample prompt comparisons (we’ve included a minimal output-diff tool in the playbook).
- Time estimate: full staged migration ~3 hours; immediate full rollback estimated 12 minutes with QA window of 20 minutes.

I’ve also added pragmatic mitigations: prefix caching bump for the payments flow and temporary adjusted batching floor for FinVoy traffic during the work. Those reduce the need for rollback and will be applied in parallel.

Attachments: fallback-playbook.md, canary-config.json

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra | Staff SRE, Redwood Inference

Thanks — I’m okay with the staged approach outlined by Rishi provided Revenue Ops signs the SLA carveout. Marissa from the account team will coordinate communications, and we’ll notify customers per the standard incident playbook if we hit the circuit-break.

Jordan — please schedule the runway (we prefer an early-morning window US-PST on 2028-12-03) and include the FinVoy SRE channel. I’ll approve the plan on the condition that the rollback can be aborted within 10 minutes if fidelity degradation is detected.

— Marissa

- Finance will log this as a non-billable SLA exception; legal/contract will be looped if FinVoy requests a longer window.

Jordan — you have authorization to execute the staged rollback per the attached playbook. Please confirm start time and post a short post-mortem within 48 hours.

— Grace
